subject: Pilot economics & spend-gate: proposed pilot scope and next steps
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot economics & spend-gate: proposed pilot scope and next steps

Ben — thanks again for walking us through ClearArc's fraud-detection flow this morning. Short recap and a suggested pilot path to validate unit economics before you open the spend gate.

What we heard (pain / goals):
- High volume of low-latency charge-authorization requests (50–200 req/s peak).
- Current rate-limiting causes ~4–6% false positives during spikes, increasing manual review load.
- Budget constraint: engineering + infra carve-out of ~$18k/mo for pilot (upper bound).
- Primary goal: reduce human review by 30% while keeping <1s p95 for decision latency.

Key levers we discussed (cost / quality):
1) Model selection & quantization: smaller decoder for hot-path decisions; fallback to larger model for edge cases.
2) Batching strategy: aggressive micro-batching for throughput during steady-state; per-request fast-path when risk score > threshold.
3) Prefix/KV caching: reuse common context for repeat customers to avoid repeated decoding.
4) Thresholding & A/B ramp: use canary split to measure manual-review reduction before full rollout.

Proposed minimal pilot (6 weeks):
- Scope: 1 region (us-west) serving auth classifier + async re-score for flagged transactions.
- Throughput target: 100 req/s sustained, 250 req/s burst; 95th latency SLO <= 1s.
- Success metrics: >=30% reduction in manual reviews OR 20% savings in ops cost + no degradation in fraud catch rate (delta <2%).
- Budget: target <= $18k/mo. We expect ~18–25% reduction vs naive hosted setup using batching + caching.

Attached: pilot-scope PDF and a token-econ worksheet with baseline assumptions.

Immediate next steps:
- You: confirm pilot budget envelope and preferred start window (Aug 31 / Sep 7).
- Us: produce a short TCO estimate with batching/caching knobs and a pilot runbook (deliverable: 2–3 page exec brief).
- If budget is tight: prioritize a 3-week discovery with performance profiling (lower cost, narrower scope).

Would you be open to a 30-min follow-up Thursday to lock scope?

Thanks,
Diego
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Ben — great, thanks. Quick baseline assumptions (high level) so procurement has numbers to react to — we'll follow with a short TCO spreadsheet tailored to ClearArc before the Thu call.

Baseline assumptions used for estimate: (conservative)
- Request profile: 100 req/s steady, 250 req/s peak (10% of requests are long-context re-scores).
- Avg input tokens per request: 40 tokens; avg output tokens: 6 tokens.
- Candidate models: Medium param open decoder for hot-path (~4–6B quantized) + large model (13B q4) for edge re-score.
- Batching: 25–40ms batching window for hot-path during steady-state (saves ~30% GPU time vs per-request).
- Caching: expected cache hit-rate 18–22% for repeat customer contexts in first pass.
- Pricing assumptions: Redwood hosted pilot estimate uses per-token + per-inference unit; combined effective unit cost after batching/caching reduced ~18–25% vs naive per-request baseline in our example.

What we'll deliver before Thu:
1) 2-page TCO memo with numbers plugged into the attached token-econ worksheet (line items: infra, requests, operator time savings).
2) Short runbook skeleton (incident + escalation steps) for your fraud ops team.
3) Pilot timeline + milestones (instrumentation, canary, evaluation).

If procurement needs an SOW stub now I can attach a one-pager; otherwise we'll bring the full TCO and SOW examples on Thu.

Marissa, Karthik — feel free to add specific quantization / runtime notes for the memo.

Diego

Ben — quick technical add from runtime side to make the TCO numbers defensible:
- We can ship a hot-path quantization profile that reduces memory bandwidth and latency (q4_0 for the 4–6B model) with minimal accuracy loss. That improves batching efficiency by ~10–15%.
- For the pilot we recommend an adaptive batching policy: small window for requests with explicit fraud indicators (0–10ms), slightly larger window (30–40ms) for unlabeled traffic. That keeps p95 latency near your 1s SLO while capturing batching benefits.
- Instrumentation: we'll surface token-level cost and a per-route latency breakdown into your console. Procurement likes concrete observability hooks (cost/latency per 1k requests) — we can add that to the SOW.
